subject.title: fix(plugins): plugins.deny is bypassed by a mixed-case manifest id

question: Should OpenClaw formally treat manifest-declared plugin IDs as case-insensitive identifiers whose canonical runtime and configuration form is lowercase, including for existing external plugins?
rationale: The security bypass needs a central repair, but lowercasing at parse time changes externally observable identity for any existing mixed-case plugin; repository-wide lowercase practice is strong evidence but is not by itself an explicit compatibility contract.

options.title: Adopt Canonical Lowercase IDs
options.body: Keep the parse-boundary repair, require focused manifest/runtime identity coverage and live Gateway denial proof, and document lowercase as the canonical plugin-ID form.

options.title: Preserve Manifest Spelling
options.body: Keep case-preserving registry identity and make every policy and reserved-ID comparison case-insensitive, accepting the maintenance risk of multiple comparison boundaries.

options.title: Reject Mixed-Case Manifests
options.body: Validate mixed-case IDs as invalid and provide clear diagnostics and upgrade guidance, which is stricter and more disruptive for existing plugins.

recommendation.title: Adopt Canonical Lowercase IDs
recommendation.body: Keep the parse-boundary repair, require focused manifest/runtime identity coverage and live Gateway denial proof, and document lowercase as the canonical plugin-ID form.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior manifest and plugin-install history is closest to the compatibility contract being decided.
